paper_did: Generated and optimized a special quasi‐random structure (SQS) of the PbSnTeSe high-entropy alloy (HEA) with a 64-atom FCC supercell using Monte Carlo SQS (MCSQS) within ATAT.
Conducted density-functional theory (DFT) calculations (with spin–orbit coupling) to determine the structural, electronic, and vibrational properties of the HEA.
Employed state-of-the-art methods by combining on‐the‐fly machine‐learned force fields (MLFF) with Green–Kubo molecular dynamics to calculate the lattice thermal conductivity.

Calculated thermoelectric transport coefficients—including the Seebeck coefficient, electrical conductivity (via Boltzmann transport theory using the relaxation time approximation), and power factor—for both n-type and p-type doping over the temperature range 300–700 K.
Determined the overall thermoelectric performance through the figure of merit (ZT), noting that n-type doping provided a maximum ZT of approximately 1.1 at 500 K.
paper_reported: PbSnTeSe HEA exhibits very low lattice thermal conductivity (around 0.4 W/(m·K) at 300 K) due to lattice distortion effects that slow phonon propagation.

The electronic transport calculations show that n-type doping leads to higher electrical conductivity and power factor than p-type, resulting in superior thermoelectric performance for n-type samples.

The ML force field developed on-the-fly successfully reproduced key structural properties and produced converged heat-flux autocorrelation functions, confirming its reliability for predicting phonon dynamics in HEAs.
paper_proposed: While not outlined in a dedicated future-work section, the paper hints at improving thermoelectric performance by further alloying (e.g., adding additional elements) to enhance electrical conductivity.

The potential exists to explore modifications and refinements in computational protocols, though the paper itself focused on defect‐free, single-phase models without explicitly addressing extrinsic factors such as grain boundaries or local lattice distortion descriptors.

paper_did: Fabricated porous (Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2Zr0.2Hf0.2)C high‐entropy ceramics via an in situ carbothermal reduction and pressureless sintering process.

Tailored the pore structure by adding varying amounts of SiO2 microspheres to generate a dual‐porosity architecture with small pores (0.4–3 μm) originating from the carbothermal reaction and large pores (20–50 μm) from the template removal.

Processed the ceramics under controlled conditions (i.e., pressureless sintering at high temperature, HF etching of the SiO2), and characterized the phase, microstructure (XRD, TEM, SEM), compressive strength, and thermal conductivity of the samples.
paper_reported: Porous HECs exhibited a dual-porosity structure that allowed tuning of thermal conductivity (from 4.12 to 1.11 W·m−1K−1) and compressive strength (from 133.1 MPa to 41.9 MPa) by controlling the SiO2 content and hence the porosity.

The excellent properties were attributed to a synergy between high-entropy effects (severe lattice distortion leading to reduced phonon mean free path) and the dual-porosity structure (providing additional interfaces for phonon scattering and crack deflection).
paper_proposed: The study proposed that the fabrication method is a universal approach to prepare HECs with controllable pore architectures, enabling tunable mechanical and thermal properties and potential application in thermal protection systems (TPS).

hypotheses.hypothesis: A predictive approach that integrates quantitative metrics of mixing entropy and atomic size mismatch (i.e., a 'lattice distortion factor') can accurately forecast low phonon thermal conductivity in high‐entropy alloys by capturing the effects of severe lattice distortions on phonon scattering.

hypotheses.structural_mediator: Severe atomic-scale lattice distortions arising from the presence of multiple principal elements with different atomic radii.
hypotheses.mechanism: Greater atomic size mismatch increases lattice strain and disorder, which shortens the phonon mean free path by enhancing scattering. This builds on the mechanism observed in high-entropy ceramics, where severe lattice distortion was linked to reduced thermal conductivity (see PMC10052925::web::010 and PMC10052925::web::016).

hypotheses.boundary: The model applies only to single-phase, homogeneous HEAs. If the alloy composition leads to phase segregation or excessive defects (beyond point disorder), the predictive correlation may break down.
hypotheses.uncertainty: While the qualitative trend is supported, the exact percentage reduction (20–30%) is an approximate target based on analogous ceramic systems with severe lattice distortion.

paper_did: Fabricated porous high‐entropy (Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2Zr0.2Hf0.2)C ceramics using an in situ carbothermal reduction route combined with pressureless sintering.

Introduced dual‐porosity by using two pore‐generation mechanisms – small pores (0.4–3 μm) formed during the carbothermal reaction and large pores (20–50 μm) created via the incorporation/etching of SiO2 microspheres (varied from 0 to 20 wt.%).

Processed the samples through uniaxial pressing, sintering at high temperatures, and characterized the materials via XRD, TEM, SEM, mercury porosimetry, compressive strength tests, and thermal conductivity measurements.
paper_reported: The ceramics exhibited a dual‐porosity structure where the porosity increased with SiO2 content – leading to tailored pore sizes and distributions.

Tunable mechanical and thermal properties were achieved, with compressive strengths ranging from 133.1 MPa (low porosity) to 41.9 MPa (high porosity) and room‐temperature thermal conductivity decreasing from 4.12 to 1.11 W·m−1·K−1.

The excellent performance was attributed to the synergistic effects of high‐entropy (severe lattice distortions that reduce phonon mean free path) and the dual‐porosity structure (which enhances phonon scattering and deflects crack propagation).
paper_proposed: The study suggests that the dual‐porosity concept, combined with high‐entropy effects, provides a universal approach to tuning thermal insulation and mechanical strength and that such materials are promising for aerospace thermal protection systems.
It implies that further tuning of the pore structure (by adjusting the type and amount of pore‐forming agents) could optimize the balance between thermal conductivity and mechanical performance.

paper_did: Developed porous (Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2Zr0.2Hf0.2)C high‐entropy ceramics by first preparing an amorphous precursor (via a solvothermal route using metal chlorides and furfuryl alcohol) and then forming a dual‐porosity structure using in situ carbothermal reduction (yielding small pores, 0.4–3 μm) together with SiO2 microspheres as sacrificial templates (creating large pores, 20–50 μm).

Varied the amount of SiO2 pore-former (0 to 20 wt.%) to tailor the overall porosity (23.08%–59.34%) and pore-size distribution, and subsequently controlled the compressive strength (133.1–41.9 MPa) and thermal conductivity (4.12–1.11 W·m−1·K−1) of the final ceramics.

Characterized the microstructure and phase purity with XRD, SEM, TEM/HAADF, and EDS, as well as the pore morphology (via mercury porosimetry) and measured thermal and mechanical properties through laser flash analysis and compressive tests.
paper_reported: The porous HECs exhibit a dual-porosity structure where small pores (from the carbothermal reaction) and large pores (from SiO2 removal) synergistically enhance phonon scattering, leading to low thermal conductivity, while the presence of small pores also helps deflect crack propagation to yield good compressive strength.

The severe lattice distortions inherent to the high-entropy carbide (due to diverse metal cations) were identified as key in reducing the intrinsic phonon mean free path and in improving thermal insulation.

A universal model for predicting thermal conductivity in porous ceramics was validated, with the measured data fitting well when appropriate parameters (e.g. shape factors, effective conductivities) were chosen.
paper_proposed: That the fabrication method—combining in situ carbothermal reduction with a sacrificial SiO2 pore-former—is a versatile, universal approach for preparing high‐entropy ceramics with tailorable pore structures and tunable thermo‐mechanical properties suitable for aerospace thermal protection applications.
That modulating the pore morphology (dual-porosity) offers a pathway to optimize the balance between thermal insulation and mechanical strength.

paper_did: Synthesized equiatomic polycrystalline and single‐crystal samples of the FCC HEA FeCoCrMnNi and confirmed its FCC structure via neutron diffraction.

Performed inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and inelastic x‐ray scattering (IXS) experiments to measure the generalized vibrational density of states (GVDOS) and individual acoustic phonon properties (dispersion, linewidth, and lifetime) in various crystallographic directions and polarizations.

Extracted and analyzed phonon linewidths (indicative of phonon lifetimes) and identified that despite the strong chemical disorder, long‐propagating acoustic phonons are present over the entire Brillouin zone, with force‐constant fluctuations (≈20%) dominating the phonon scattering.
paper_reported: Observed that the acoustic phonon dispersions in FeCoCrMnNi closely follow those of the constituent pure elements and binary alloys, though with notably reduced lifetimes due to disorder.

Reported anisotropic phonon broadening with longitudinal modes showing multiple regimes (e.g., a (ℏω)^4.5 energy dependence at low energies) and transverse modes displaying a smoother monotonic increase, strongly linked to force‐constant fluctuations.

Identified that the onset of strong scattering in the HEA is correlated with the deviation of the GVDOS from Debye behavior and that, unlike in glasses or complex metallic alloys, a broad acoustic regime persists up to high energies and wavevectors.
paper_proposed: Suggested the need for further theoretical and modeling work to incorporate anisotropic scattering mechanisms and to use the experimental phonon data as benchmarks for improved predictive models of polyatomic random alloys.

Proposed that better phonon engineering might be achieved by selecting elements with larger differences (to enhance force‐constant fluctuations) and by exploring different crystallographic structures (e.g., HCP/BCC HEAs), although such modifications introduce additional complexities.

paper_did: Fabricated rare‐earth‐zirconate porous high-entropy ceramics ((La0.25Eu0.25Gd0.25Yb0.25)2(Zr0.75Ce0.25)2O7) via a TBA-based gel-casting method using nanoscale powders (RE2O3, ZrO2, CeO2) calcined at 1200 °C.
Varied the initial solid loading (5–15 vol%) to control and tailor the pore structure of the ceramics.
Processed the materials through gelation, drying, debinding, and sintering at 1500 °C, and characterized the resulting ceramics using XRD, HRTEM, SEM, Raman spectroscopy, TG-DSC, and porosimetry.

Tested and quantified key properties including high porosity (67.1–81.5%), moderate compressive strength (1.02–6.45 MPa), and low thermal conductivity (0.0642–0.1213 W/(m·K) at room temperature and 0.1467 W/(m·K) at 1200 °C).
paper_reported: The ceramics exhibit a single-phase fluorite structure with uniform, open-cell pore distributions and grain sizes around 1 μm.
Tailored pore structures effectively reduce heat transfer via mechanisms such as Mie scattering, leading to exceptional thermal insulation performance.
A clear correlation was observed: lower solid loading yielded higher porosity and lower thermal conductivity, while higher loadings increased compressive strength.
paper_proposed: The work suggests that optimizing pore structure—by simply varying initial solid loadings—offers a promising route to further enhance the thermal insulation performance of rare-earth-zirconate porous high-entropy ceramics.
It points to the potential for these ceramics to be used as high-temperature thermal insulation materials, thereby motivating further studies on pore structure tailoring and compositional design.

paper_did: Developed a data‐driven ML approach to predict phase formation in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) using a dataset of 5,692 experimental observations that was later balanced via synthetic data augmentation (approximately 1,500 records per phase category).

Employed multiple ML algorithms (XGBoost, Random Forest, SVC, and ANNs) to classify HEA phases across 11 distinct phase categories (including single-phase solid solutions and mixtures involving intermetallic and amorphous phases).

Conducted extensive data cleaning, feature generation (using descriptors such as mixing entropy, mixing enthalpy, valence electron count, atomic size difference, and electronegativity measures), and performed a detailed feature importance analysis to assess which descriptors best predict phase outcomes.
Investigated how the inclusion of additional phase types (IM and AM) affects overall prediction accuracy and model-specific feature rankings.
paper_reported: High prediction accuracies were achieved by the ML models, with tuned XGBoost and Random Forest reaching up to 97% accuracy for solid solution phases and about 86% accuracy when all 11 phase categories were considered.

Model-specific variations were observed in feature importance; for example, XGBoost ranked mixing entropy, electronegativity deviation, VEC, and mixing enthalpy as top predictors, while RF emphasized features such as average electronegativity and the number of valence electrons.

Synthetic data augmentation was successfully used to balance class representation in the dataset, and its inclusion was shown to have only a minimal (<1%) improvement effect on overall model accuracy.

The work underscored that ML predictions for HEA phase formation are sensitive to both the chosen algorithm and the phase mix considered, motivating careful model and feature selection for targeted alloy design.
paper_proposed: Future work was suggested in terms of further refining ML model selection and feature extraction techniques to improve predictions for complex, multi-phase HEAs.

There is an implicit proposal to apply the insights from feature importance analysis to tailor alloy design strategies (e.g., guiding composition choices) although the study did not extend to predicting material properties beyond phase formation.

An extension toward addressing the challenges of imbalanced datasets and expanding the predictive framework (e.g., through additional synthetic data augmentation) was highlighted for enhanced reliability in HEA design.

paper_did: Developed a machine‐learning approach using a binary alloy dataset generated via DFT (using KKR-CPA) to classify crystal structural phases (bcc, fcc, hcp) of all‐d-metal alloys.
Introduced a feature transformation that converts raw electronic descriptors {nd, σd} into low-dimensional, expandable features {ndex, σdex} via ensemble trees and weighted pooling.
Integrated compositional descriptors (e.g., atomic size difference δ) into the prediction model and trained a support vector machine (SVM) on the binary dataset.

Validated the method by applying the binary-trained model to predict experimental multi-element alloys (including HEAs and ternary alloys) and demonstrated comparable prediction accuracy (∼80–84%) with drastically reduced computational cost.
paper_reported: The transformed features {ndex, σdex} (with δ) achieved comparable accuracy to raw features, reporting ∼80.56% accuracy for experimental multi-element alloys and ∼84.20% for HEAs.
The misclassification issues were predominantly observed between the fcc and hcp phases.
The work demonstrated that using binary alloy data to build the training set cuts computational cost by over three orders of magnitude compared to generating multi-element (HEA) training data.
paper_proposed: Future work combining the predictive approach with further experiments to discover new multi-element alloys (including solid solution HEAs).
Expansion of the method to screen for unknown solid solution phases and potential multi-phase or intermetallic alloy systems using training results from binary alloy data.

paper_reported: Reported prediction accuracies of around 81% with raw features and approximately 78–80% with the transformed expandable features for binary alloys, with experimental multi-element alloy predictions reaching about 80.56% (and 84.20% for HEAs).

Showed that the use of expandable features reduces the required computational cost for the training set by more than three orders of magnitude compared to full raw-feature training in HEA compositional space.

paper_did: Developed and applied a supervised machine‐learning strategy that combines multiple regression/CCA analysis with a genetic algorithm (GA) to screen the vast compositional space of high‐entropy (multi‐principal element) alloys.

Compiled a database of 82 experimentally synthesized HE alloys with measured Vicker’s hardness and computed several alloy metrics (e.g., mixing entropy, mixing enthalpy, radius asymmetry, valence electron concentration) from their compositions.
Used the GA with evolutionary processes (selection, recombination, mutation) to generate candidate alloy compositions and tuned the GA parameters over many (≥1000) generations.
Synthesized seven candidate alloys via arc-melting and characterized them by Vicker’s hardness testing, SEM imaging, and EDS mapping to validate predicted mechanical properties.
Assessed ductility using the Pugh criterion and optical inspection of micro-hardness indentation cracks, linking compositional metrics to both hardness and phase behavior.
paper_reported: A strong correlation (r ≈ 0.79, p ≈ 0) between a reduced set of compositional descriptors (ΔSmix, ΔHmix, VEC) and measured hardness was established, suggesting that increased compositional disorder (high ΔSmix) and a lower mixing enthalpy/VEC promote higher hardness.
Two candidate alloys exhibited extremely high Vicker’s hardness (exceeding 1000 HV) as predicted by the fitness function from the multi-regression/CCA analysis and validated experimentally.

Microstructural and microchemical analyses revealed dendritic structures with distinct elemental segregation patterns that helped explain the differences in hardness and ductility among the synthesized HE alloys.
The GA screenings, combined with the regression analysis, reliably identified promising alloy compositions and demonstrated the utility of data analytics in accelerating HE alloy design.
paper_proposed: Extend the data analytics approach to incorporate additional properties beyond hardness, such as yield strength, electrical conductivity, corrosion resistance, and processing/property correlations.
Explore the influence of minor compositional perturbations and additional descriptors on alloy properties to further fine-tune predictions.
Implement multi-objective (Pareto) optimization that simultaneously considers mechanical properties (e.g., hardness and ductility via the Pugh criterion) and potentially other performance metrics.

hypotheses.structural_mediator: Increased mass disorder promotes phonon scattering at the atomic scale.
hypotheses.mechanism: Large disparities in atomic masses among elements increase the scattering of phonons, reducing the mean free path and thus lowering the lattice thermal conductivity. Integrating these vibrational descriptors into the prediction algorithm should capture this effect more effectively than traditional compositional metrics alone.

hypotheses.boundary: This enhancement is expected to work for single-phase, well-mixed HEAs; multi-phase systems with complex segregations may limit its applicability.
hypotheses.uncertainty: The precise quantitative improvement in prediction accuracy is uncertain and may vary with the dataset size and alloy system.

hypotheses.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys produced as single-phase solid solutions by arc melting, where traditional models primarily addressing average compositional metrics have been used.
hypotheses.intervention: Enhance the predictive model by adding descriptors quantifying the extent of chemical short-range ordering (using, for example, indicators derived from pair correlation functions or scattering parameters) alongside vibrational disorder metrics (such as mass variance). hypotheses.structural_mediator: Nano-scale chemical clusters act as additional scattering centers for phonons, thereby shortening the phonon mean free path without necessarily compromising overall phase stability and mechanical properties.
hypotheses.mechanism: Even in an overall single-phase alloy, subtle short-range order can result in regions of slightly different bonding environments. hypotheses.predicted_outcome: The predictive approach is expected to identify HEA compositions that, when synthesized, exhibit a reduction in phonon thermal conductivity of roughly 15% or more compared to alloys selected without consideration of SRO, while maintaining acceptable mechanical integrity.

paper_did: Collected and curated a large database (up to 614 HEAs) and derived a set of physically‐meaningful phenomenological parameters (e.g., PFPA1, PFPA2, PFPA3, PFPB2, PSP, PFPSigma, and PFPLaves) from binary phase diagrams.
Employed a machine learning (Random Forest) approach to classify HEA phase formation (including disordered FCC, BCC, HCP, mixed phases, and intermetallic phases) using these parameters.
Synthesized 42 new HEAs via suction casting (with as-cast and high‐temperature annealing conditions above 0.7Tm) to experimentally validate the predictive capability of the model.
paper_reported: The ML-based predictive approach yielded high prediction accuracies (above 80–90%) in classifying HEA phases across different database levels.

Clear correlations were established between the calculated binary phase diagram–inspired parameters (e.g., PFPA1, PFPA2, PSP, etc.) and the resultant phase formations, confirming that binary interactions encode information on atomic mixing and phase separation.
Experimental validation with 42 newly synthesized HEAs confirmed that the model can accurately predict phase formation even for compositions beyond the current known phase regions.
paper_proposed: Enhancing the model by incorporating additional physical parameters (such as mixing enthalpy) into the ML framework to further refine phase predictions.
Integrating the binary phase diagram–based approach with complementary methods (e.g., CALPHAD) for detailed phase-field analysis and microstructural control.
Expanding the study to consider additional phases (e.g., line compounds, minor phases) and adapting the approach to diverse processing methods.

hypotheses.hypothesis: HEAs predicted to exhibit high phase separation parameters (PSP) by the binary phase diagram‐inspired predictive approach will achieve lower phonon thermal conductivity due to enhanced phonon scattering at numerous heterogeneous phase boundaries.
hypotheses.material_initial_state: An as-cast high-entropy alloy (HEA) with a relatively homogeneous disordered solid solution structure prepared by suction casting.
hypotheses.intervention: Select and synthesize HEAs whose binary phase diagram analysis yields high PSP values and then, if needed, apply a high-temperature annealing treatment (above 0.7Tm) to stabilize the microstructure.
hypotheses.conditions: Samples are produced under controlled conditions (suction casting followed by annealing above 0.7Tm) to lock in the microstructural heterogeneity predicted by high PSP.
hypotheses.structural_mediator: Enhanced phase separation leads to microstructural heterogeneity with a high density of interfaces and local compositional fluctuations.
hypotheses.mechanism: High PSP values indicate pronounced phase separation in binary subsystems. In such microstructures, a high density of phase boundaries and compositional inhomogeneities strongly scatter phonons, reducing their mean free path. This increased phonon scattering decreases the lattice thermal conductivity, thereby improving the material’s insulation performance.
hypotheses.predicted_outcome: Compared to conventional HEAs with lower PSP, the predicted HEAs should show a measurable reduction in phonon thermal conductivity (tentatively estimated improvement of around 15–20% lower k) under the same test conditions.
hypotheses.baseline: Standard as-cast or annealed HEAs with modest PSP values, exhibiting typical phonon thermal conductivities expected from disordered solid solutions.
hypotheses.boundary: This correlation is expected to hold for HEAs processed by suction casting and high-temperature annealing (≥0.7Tm) where binary phase diagram parameters directly encode atomic interactions; it may not apply to mechanically alloyed HEAs or those with distinct nanostructured reinforcements.
hypotheses.uncertainty: Exact magnitude of thermal conductivity improvement is uncertain; estimated reduction is qualitative and requires experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of HEAs with similar bulk compositions but differing PSP values (one group predicted with high PSP and one with moderate PSP) using identical processing routes. Carefully measure the lattice-dominated phonon thermal conductivity using steady-state or laser flash methods.
measurements: Quantitative measurements of thermal conductivity (k) at relevant temperatures.
Microstructural analysis (e.g., XRD and TEM) to confirm phase separation and interface density.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEAs with high predicted PSP do not show a statistically significant (e.g., >10–15%) reduction in phonon thermal conductivity compared to the control group, or if microstructural analysis does not reveal increased phase boundaries, the hypothesis is falsified.

hypotheses.what_is_new: Applies the predictive approach to correlate PSP not only with phase formation but specifically with enhanced phonon scattering and reduced thermal conductivity for thermal insulation applications.

hypotheses.hypothesis: HEAs that are predicted to exhibit significant intermetallic (IM+) phase fractions via the binary phase diagram predictive parameters (PFPSigma and PFPLaves) will show lower phonon thermal conductivity due to nanoscale second phase inclusions causing enhanced phonon scattering.
hypotheses.material_initial_state: A multicomponent HEA synthesized in the as-cast state where the predictive analysis indicates the likelihood of mixed phases with intermetallic (IM+) character.
hypotheses.intervention: Tailor the alloy composition using the predictive model to increase the PFPSigma and PFPLaves parameters so that a controlled fraction of fine intermetallic precipitates (or IM+ phases) forms during solidification.
hypotheses.conditions: The HEA is synthesized under controlled casting conditions; minimal post-processing is applied to preserve the predicted mixed-phase microstructure. Testing is done at room temperature and elevated temperatures relevant to insulation applications.
hypotheses.structural_mediator: The formation of nanoscale IM+ inclusions generates numerous coherent or semi-coherent interfaces within the matrix.
hypotheses.mechanism: The binary phase diagram–based parameters PFPSigma and PFPLaves are used to predict the formation of intermetallic phases within HEAs. The presence of fine intermetallic precipitates, distributed uniformly in the matrix, acts as phonon scattering centers. The interfaces between the matrix and these precipitates disrupt the propagation of phonons, lowering the lattice thermal conductivity.
hypotheses.predicted_outcome: HEAs with higher predicted IM+ content should exhibit lower phonon thermal conductivity, with an anticipated improvement on the order of a 20% reduction in k relative to similar compositions with fewer intermetallic phases.
hypotheses.baseline: Conventional HEAs predicted by the approach to form predominantly single-phase solid solutions (e.g., FCC or BCC) without significant intermetallic formation.
hypotheses.boundary: This approach applies in regimes where intermetallic phases can form without compromising mechanical stability. It might be limited if excessive IM formation leads to embrittlement or if processing conditions (e.g., rapid solidification) suppress intermetallic precipitation.
hypotheses.uncertainty: The precise volume fraction and size distribution required for optimal phonon scattering is not accurately predicted a priori, and the expected reduction magnitude (~20%) is an estimate subject to experimental validation.

Quantitative phase analysis using XRD/TEM to determine intermetallic volume fraction and distribution.

hypotheses.conditions: Samples are processed via casting followed by controlled annealing at Tpf to maximize the coexistence of FCC and BCC phases; tests are conducted at temperatures typical for thermal insulation applications.
hypotheses.structural_mediator: A finely intermixed microstructure consisting of FCC and BCC domains with nanoscale phase boundaries and local lattice misfit strains.
hypotheses.mechanism: According to the predictive approach, similar magnitude values of PFPA1 and PFPA2 favor the formation of mixed-phase HEAs. The coexistence of FCC and BCC regions leads to internal strain fields and an abundance of phase boundaries. These defects and disordered interfaces serve as effective phonon scattering centers, thereby reducing lattice thermal conductivity.
hypotheses.predicted_outcome: The mixed-phase HEAs should display a lower phonon thermal conductivity relative to more homogeneous single-phase HEAs, with an estimated reduction potentially on the order of 10–15% compared to conventional predictions for single solid solutions.
hypotheses.baseline: HEAs with dominant single-phase (either FCC or BCC) microstructures that typically show higher thermal conductivity due to more uniform lattice structures.
hypotheses.boundary: The hypothesis holds for HEAs where the phase fractions can be deliberately balanced via composition and annealing; it may not apply if phase separation is too extreme or if one phase dominates entirely.
hypotheses.uncertainty: Quantitative estimates of conductivity reduction are tentative; the exact influence of local strain and boundary density on phonon scattering may vary with composition and processing nuances.

fields.hypothesis: Integrating local lattice distortion descriptors derived from DFT and ML force-field simulations into the predictive model will enable more accurate identification of HEAs with low phonon thermal conductivity.
fields.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) with a single-phase FCC structure and moderate atomic disorder (similar to PbSnTeSe).
fields.intervention: Develop a predictive model that, in addition to overall composition, incorporates quantitative descriptors of local lattice distortions (such as bond-length distributions and coordination variance) obtained from high-fidelity DFT and on‐the‐fly ML force field simulations.
fields.conditions: Applicable to HEAs composed of 4–5 principal elements in near equiatomic ratios and operating in the temperature range of 300–700 K.
fields.structural_mediator: Local distortions and mass fluctuation-induced scattering centers in the crystal lattice.
fields.mechanism: In HEAs, lattice distortions increase phonon scattering and reduce the mean free path. By using local structural descriptors, the predictive model can more precisely account for how these distortions impede phonon propagation, leading to low lattice thermal conductivity.
fields.predicted_outcome: The approach should predict lattice thermal conductivities with a reduced error margin (within ~10–20%) compared to conventional models that use only global composition parameters.
fields.baseline: Existing predictive models that rely on macroscopic descriptors (e.g., overall composition or averaged melting points) without explicit local structural detail.
fields.boundary: The method is expected to work reliably for single-phase, disordered HEAs with moderate configurational entropy and may not extend trivially to ordered alloys or multiphase systems.
fields.uncertainty: The exact percentage improvement in prediction accuracy is uncertain due to complexities in quantifying local distortions across different HEA systems.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of HEAs with controlled variations in local lattice distortions. Measure their lattice thermal conductivities (using techniques such as time-domain thermoreflectance) over 300–700 K and compare the measured values with the predictions from the new model.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted lattice thermal conductivities differ by more than 20% from the measured values across the samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.

pool.builds_on: The on‐the‐fly ML force field method introduced in the paper (PMC9822225::web::016) is extended here to include explicit temperature re-adaptation for improved anharmonic capture.
pool.what_is_new: This hypothesis proposes a dynamic, temperature-adaptive training regime for ML force fields specifically aimed at capturing anharmonic effects, which were not accounted for in the paper.

fields.hypothesis: A temperature-adaptive predictive approach employing on‐the‐fly ML force fields will capture anharmonic phonon interactions more accurately, thereby improving predictions of low lattice thermal conductivity in HEAs.
fields.material_initial_state: Defect-free, single-phase HEAs with high configurational entropy similar to those studied in PbSnTeSe.
fields.intervention: Implement an on‐the‐fly ML force field that is continuously re-trained over a range of temperatures to account for temperature-dependent anharmonic effects, and use this model in molecular dynamics simulations to predict κL.
fields.conditions: Applicable to HEAs operating in the 300–700 K temperature range, where anharmonic phonon scattering becomes significant.
fields.structural_mediator: Enhanced anharmonic phonon-phonon scattering due to temperature-induced lattice vibrations.

pool.label: C14
pool.builds_on: The GA and regression-based screening methodologies demonstrated in the paper for alloy hardness, repurposed here to target thermal insulation by focusing on vibrational (phonon) properties while addressing the limitation of high electronic conductivity in metallic HEAs.
pool.what_is_new: This hypothesis explicitly incorporates an electronic descriptor alongside vibrational metrics to tailor the prediction for low phonon thermal conductivity, selecting alloy compositions where the typically dominant electron conduction is minimized—an aspect not addressed in the original paper.

fields.hypothesis: In HEAs with intrinsically lower electronic thermal conductivity (achieved by selecting elements with lower conduction electron densities), a predictive approach that integrates both lattice vibrational descriptors (e.g., atomic mass variance, local Debye temperature variations) and an explicit electronic conductivity descriptor (such as estimated electron density or effective mass) will more accurately identify alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity for thermal insulation applications.
fields.material_initial_state: Single‐phase high-entropy alloys that are conventionally optimized in metallic systems (e.g., similar to CoCrFeNiCu) but where the alloy chemistry is adjusted to yield reduced free-electron density.
fields.intervention: Modify the predictive model to include additional descriptors that capture both lattice vibrational disorder (atomic mass variance, local Debye temperature disparities) and estimated electronic conduction parameters (e.g., conduction electron density or effective electron mass) so that the predictive framework emphasizes systems where the lattice (phonon) component dominates the overall heat conduction.
fields.conditions: The approach is applicable to HEAs synthesized in a single-phase regime at room temperature, with compositions chosen such that the electronic contribution is minimized. Experimental thermal conductivity measurements (isolating phonon contributions, e.g., via temperature-dependent studies) should be performed on arc-melted alloys under well-controlled microstructural homogeneity.
fields.structural_mediator: Enhanced atomic-scale mass and bonding disorder in alloys with lower conduction electron density increases phonon scattering while the suppressed electronic heat conduction ensures that the phonon thermal conductivity dominates the overall thermal insulation behavior.
fields.mechanism: Lower free-electron densities reduce the electronic thermal transport channel, allowing the effects of vibrational disorder to become the key factor in thermal insulation. Incorporating both vibrational and electronic descriptors captures the competition between lattice and electron conduction, ensuring that the predictive model selects alloys where enhanced phonon scattering (due to mass variance and bond strength variations) effectively lowers the thermal conductivity.
fields.predicted_outcome: The revised model is expected to improve the accuracy of identifying HEAs with low phonon thermal conductivity (by roughly 15–20% over models using only traditional alloy metrics) in systems where the electronic contribution is inherently low.
fields.baseline: A predictive approach that employs conventional compositional and mechanical metrics (as in the paper’s GA/CCA method) without separating vibrational and electronic contributions.
fields.boundary: This hypothesis is most applicable to HEAs that can be compositionally tuned to have lower free-electron densities. In systems where the electronic contribution dominates (typical of most metals), the vibrational descriptors alone would be insufficient.
fields.uncertainty: The exact quantitative improvement in prediction accuracy is uncertain and sensitive to the effectiveness of the electronic descriptor integration, as well as the accuracy of isolating phonon thermal conductivity from total conductivity in experiments.

falsification_experiment.design: Develop two predictive models: one that integrates both vibrational and electronic descriptors and a conventional model that does not. Use each model to select candidate HEAs with purposely lowered electron density. Synthesize a statistically significant set of alloys and measure their phonon-specific thermal conductivity (using temperature-dependence or other separation techniques) along with electronic transport properties.

pool.label: C15
pool.builds_on: The GA-based selection strategy from the paper, extended by incorporating nanoscale microstructural descriptors that influence phonon scattering.
pool.what_is_new: This hypothesis introduces the concept of nano-scale chemical short-range ordering as a deliberate descriptor in the predictive framework, aiming to capture additional phonon scattering mechanisms not addressed by average compositional metrics in the original work.

fields.hypothesis: A dual-descriptor predictive approach that incorporates measures of nano-scale chemical short-range order (SRO) and vibrational disorder will enable the identification of HEAs with inherently low phonon thermal conductivity, by leveraging the additional phonon scattering induced by sub-micron chemical clustering.
fields.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys produced as single-phase solid solutions by arc melting, where traditional models primarily addressing average compositional metrics have been used.
fields.intervention: Enhance the predictive model by adding descriptors quantifying the extent of chemical short-range ordering (using, for example, indicators derived from pair correlation functions or scattering parameters) alongside vibrational disorder metrics (such as mass variance). These descriptors should be integrated into the GA’s fitness function to guide the optimization toward compositions that favor nano-scale clustering.
fields.conditions: Applicable to HEAs that are processed to ensure minimal macro segregation (e.g., through repeated remelting) so that any detected chemical ordering is at the nano-scale. Subsequent experimental characterization must include high-resolution microscopy (TEM/EDS) and phonon thermal conductivity measurements (laser flash or time-domain thermoreflectance) at room temperature.
fields.structural_mediator: Nano-scale chemical clusters act as additional scattering centers for phonons, thereby shortening the phonon mean free path without necessarily compromising overall phase stability and mechanical properties.
fields.mechanism: Even in an overall single-phase alloy, subtle short-range order can result in regions of slightly different bonding environments. This heterogeneous structure increases phonon scattering, and when combined with inherent vibrational disorder due to mass mismatch, leads to a lower lattice thermal conductivity.
fields.predicted_outcome: The predictive approach is expected to identify HEA compositions that, when synthesized, exhibit a reduction in phonon thermal conductivity of roughly 15% or more compared to alloys selected without consideration of SRO, while maintaining acceptable mechanical integrity.
fields.baseline: Standard predictive models that optimize alloy properties based solely on average metrics (mixing enthalpy, entropy, VEC) without explicit consideration of nano-scale chemical ordering.
fields.boundary: This hypothesis applies mainly to single-phase HEAs where nano-scale chemical ordering can occur without triggering macroscopic phase separation. In alloys that form distinct secondary phases, the correlation between SRO descriptors and phonon scattering may not hold.
fields.uncertainty: The quantification of nano-scale SRO in disordered alloys is challenging, and the degree to which it affects phonon transport relative to other scattering mechanisms is not precisely known.

falsification_experiment.design: Implement the enhanced predictive model to screen for HEAs predicted to exhibit significant nano-scale SRO and high vibrational disorder. pool.label: C16
pool.builds_on: the finding in the paper that binary phase diagram–inspired parameters (PSP) reliably capture phase separation trends in HEAs
pool.what_is_new: Applies the predictive approach to correlate PSP not only with phase formation but specifically with enhanced phonon scattering and reduced thermal conductivity for thermal insulation applications.

fields.hypothesis: HEAs predicted to exhibit high phase separation parameters (PSP) by the binary phase diagram‐inspired predictive approach will achieve lower phonon thermal conductivity due to enhanced phonon scattering at numerous heterogeneous phase boundaries.
fields.material_initial_state: An as-cast high-entropy alloy (HEA) with a relatively homogeneous disordered solid solution structure prepared by suction casting.
fields.intervention: Select and synthesize HEAs whose binary phase diagram analysis yields high PSP values and then, if needed, apply a high-temperature annealing treatment (above 0.7Tm) to stabilize the microstructure.
fields.conditions: Samples are produced under controlled conditions (suction casting followed by annealing above 0.7Tm) to lock in the microstructural heterogeneity predicted by high PSP.
fields.structural_mediator: Enhanced phase separation leads to microstructural heterogeneity with a high density of interfaces and local compositional fluctuations.
fields.mechanism: High PSP values indicate pronounced phase separation in binary subsystems. In such microstructures, a high density of phase boundaries and compositional inhomogeneities strongly scatter phonons, reducing their mean free path. This increased phonon scattering decreases the lattice thermal conductivity, thereby improving the material’s insulation performance.
fields.predicted_outcome: Compared to conventional HEAs with lower PSP, the predicted HEAs should show a measurable reduction in phonon thermal conductivity (tentatively estimated improvement of around 15–20% lower k) under the same test conditions.
fields.baseline: Standard as-cast or annealed HEAs with modest PSP values, exhibiting typical phonon thermal conductivities expected from disordered solid solutions.
fields.boundary: This correlation is expected to hold for HEAs processed by suction casting and high-temperature annealing (≥0.7Tm) where binary phase diagram parameters directly encode atomic interactions; it may not apply to mechanically alloyed HEAs or those with distinct nanostructured reinforcements.
fields.uncertainty: Exact magnitude of thermal conductivity improvement is uncertain; estimated reduction is qualitative and requires experimental calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of HEAs with similar bulk compositions but differing PSP values (one group predicted with high PSP and one with moderate PSP) using identical processing routes. Carefully measure the lattice-dominated phonon thermal conductivity using steady-state or laser flash methods.
measurements: Quantitative measurements of thermal conductivity (k) at relevant temperatures.
Microstructural analysis (e.g., XRD and TEM) to confirm phase separation and interface density.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the HEAs with high predicted PSP do not show a statistically significant (e.g., >10–15%) reduction in phonon thermal conductivity compared to the control group, or if microstructural analysis does not reveal increased phase boundaries, the hypothesis is falsified.

pool.what_is_new: Proposes that deliberately engineering a balanced mixed FCC+BCC microstructure, via ML-guided predictive design using binary phase diagram parameters, can be used as a strategy to lower phonon thermal conductivity for thermal insulation applications—a concept not addressed in the original work.

fields.hypothesis: HEAs predicted by the machine learning model to form mixed single solid solution phases (e.g., a combination of FCC and BCC detected via PFPA1 and PFPA2 parameters) will exhibit reduced phonon thermal conductivity due to local lattice strain and phase-boundary disorder enhancing phonon scattering.
fields.material_initial_state: A high-entropy alloy produced via standard casting that initially exhibits a mixed-phase microstructure with both FCC and BCC regions, as indicated by PFPA1 and PFPA2 analysis.
fields.intervention: Adjust alloy composition based on the predictive model to achieve near-equal high values of PFPA1 and PFPA2, and follow with an optimized annealing treatment near the phase formation temperature (Tpf ≈ 0.8Tm) to stabilize the mixed-phase microstructure.
fields.conditions: Samples are processed via casting followed by controlled annealing at Tpf to maximize the coexistence of FCC and BCC phases; tests are conducted at temperatures typical for thermal insulation applications.
fields.structural_mediator: A finely intermixed microstructure consisting of FCC and BCC domains with nanoscale phase boundaries and local lattice misfit strains.
fields.mechanism: According to the predictive approach, similar magnitude values of PFPA1 and PFPA2 favor the formation of mixed-phase HEAs. The coexistence of FCC and BCC regions leads to internal strain fields and an abundance of phase boundaries. These defects and disordered interfaces serve as effective phonon scattering centers, thereby reducing lattice thermal conductivity.
fields.predicted_outcome: The mixed-phase HEAs should display a lower phonon thermal conductivity relative to more homogeneous single-phase HEAs, with an estimated reduction potentially on the order of 10–15% compared to conventional predictions for single solid solutions.
fields.baseline: HEAs with dominant single-phase (either FCC or BCC) microstructures that typically show higher thermal conductivity due to more uniform lattice structures.
fields.boundary: The hypothesis holds for HEAs where the phase fractions can be deliberately balanced via composition and annealing; it may not apply if phase separation is too extreme or if one phase dominates entirely.
fields.uncertainty: Quantitative estimates of conductivity reduction are tentative; the exact influence of local strain and boundary density on phonon scattering may vary with composition and processing nuances.

Carry out detailed microstructural characterization and measure phonon thermal conductivity using techniques such as time-domain thermoreflectance.
measurements: Phase fraction determination via XRD and TEM to confirm the microstructure.
Thermal conductivity measurement across a temperature range relevant to insulation applications.

top3.label: C10
top3.builds_on: The findings in the paper demonstrating that low Debye temperature and average sound velocity correlate with reduced thermal conductivity in GeTe-based HE chalcogenides.
top3.what_is_new: This hypothesis extends the paper’s mechanistic insights by integrating detailed ab initio vibrational descriptors into a predictive framework specifically targeted at high-entropy alloys for thermal insulation applications.

fields.hypothesis: Integrating ab initio–computed vibrational descriptors (such as Debye temperature, average sound velocity, and Grüneisen parameter) into a predictive model will accurately identify high-entropy chalcogenide alloys with significantly reduced phonon thermal conductivity, achieving improvements of roughly 20% over conventional empirical models.
fields.material_initial_state: High-entropy chalcogenide alloys (e.g., GeTe-based HEAs similar to the m0–m9 systems in the paper) with moderate thermal conductivity.
fields.intervention: Develop and apply a predictive approach that uses high-fidelity DFT-calculated phonon and elastic properties as input descriptors for screening candidate alloys.
fields.conditions: Calculations performed at room temperature (≈300 K) on single-phase, disordered HEAs; subsequent synthesis and measurement of lattice thermal conductivity under controlled conditions.
fields.structural_mediator: The reduction in Debye temperature and average sound velocity indicates weaker interatomic bonds and enhanced phonon scattering, which mediate lower thermal conductivity.
fields.mechanism: Alloying-induced disorder leads to measurable reductions in vibrational frequencies. When these vibrational descriptors are accurately computed and used in the predictive model, the model can select materials whose phono scattering is maximized, thereby lowering κ relative to predictions based solely on averaged empirical parameters.
fields.predicted_outcome: The predictive approach will identify alloy compositions exhibiting approximately 20% lower lattice thermal conductivity compared to predictions from traditional methods (e.g., Slack or Clarke models) that do not incorporate detailed vibrational descriptors.
fields.baseline: Traditional empirical models that use bulk parameters and averaged mass effects without capturing the detailed phonon dispersion changes.
fields.boundary: The approach should work well for single-phase, highly disordered high-entropy alloys similar in chemistry and structure to the chalcogenides studied; deviations may occur for systems with phase separation or ordering.
fields.uncertainty: While the overall trend is supported by ab initio insights, the exact percentage improvement (≈20%) has moderate uncertainty due to sensitivity to computational parameters and synthesis variations.

falsification_experiment.design: Select several candidate HEAs predicted to have low κ by the model. Synthesize these alloys and measure their lattice thermal conductivity using standard techniques (e.g., laser flash analysis).
measurements: Debye temperature via calorimetry or inelastic neutron scattering
Average sound velocity from ultrasonic measurements
Direct measurement of lattice thermal conductivity
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured thermal conductivity reductions are not at least 20% lower than those predicted by traditional methods for a statistically significant number of samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

top3.label: C13
top3.builds_on: the original work's concept of using binary alloy data and feature transformation, extended here by directly linking mass variance to vibrational properties (phonon dispersion) rather than phase information alone.
top3.what_is_new: This hypothesis explicitly calibrates a mass disorder parameter using DFT phonon dispersion data, ensuring that the descriptor is physically tied to phonon scattering mechanisms affecting thermal conductivity—an aspect not addressed in the original paper.

fields.hypothesis: Integrate a mass disorder descriptor calibrated directly from phonon dispersion data of binary alloys into the predictive framework to identify HEAs with low phonon thermal conductivity.
fields.material_initial_state: All-d-metal HEAs with near-equiatomic compositions produced by conventional melting/casting, exhibiting uniform single-phase solid solutions.
fields.intervention: Perform DFT phonon dispersion calculations on a set of binary alloys to correlate atomic mass variance with changes in vibrational density of states. Use this calibration to transform compositional mass distributions into a mass disorder parameter that is explicitly linked to phonon scattering. Incorporate this parameter into the feature set used by the machine learning model.
fields.conditions: The HEAs must remain within the transition metal regime (all-d-metal systems) and maintain homogenously mixed phases; the phonon dispersion calibration is valid only for systems where DFT reliably captures vibrational properties.
fields.structural_mediator: Enhanced phonon scattering arising from vibrational mismatches due to mass disorder, as quantified by shifts and broadenings in phonon dispersion curves.
fields.mechanism: A higher mass disorder parameter, validated through DFT phonon calculations, disrupts coherent lattice vibrations by introducing frequency mismatches. This enhanced scattering lowers the phonon thermal conductivity. Calibrating the descriptor directly from vibrational (phonon) data ensures the mechanism is physically tied to thermal transport rather than solely relying on electronic features.
fields.predicted_outcome: HEAs with higher calibrated mass disorder values will exhibit a significantly lower phonon thermal conductivity, with an anticipated improvement in insulation of roughly 15–20% compared to HEAs with lower mass disorder, within experimental uncertainties.
fields.baseline: Standard prediction methods that use only electronic ({ndex, σdex}) and size-difference (δ) features from binary alloys, which do not account for vibrational effects explicitly.
fields.boundary: This approach is applicable to all-d-metal HEAs where DFT captures phonon behavior reliably. It may not extend to systems with significant contributions from p or f electrons or cases with segregation that affects vibrational modes.
fields.uncertainty: While DFT phonon dispersion is well-established for binary systems, transferring the calibration to multi-component HEAs may introduce quantitative uncertainties; the exact percentage reduction might vary with experimental processing.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of HEAs chosen based on predicted mass disorder parameter values (one with high and one with low values). Validate their phases via XRD and microscopy. Use laser flash analysis to measure their phonon thermal conductivities and compare against the predictions.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If HEAs predicted to have high mass disorder do not exhibit at least a 15% lower phonon thermal conductivity compared to the low mass disorder group, the hypothesis is falsified.

top3.label: C15
top3.builds_on: The GA-based selection strategy from the paper, extended by incorporating nanoscale microstructural descriptors that influence phonon scattering.
top3.what_is_new: This hypothesis introduces the concept of nano-scale chemical short-range ordering as a deliberate descriptor in the predictive framework, aiming to capture additional phonon scattering mechanisms not addressed by average compositional metrics in the original work.

fields.hypothesis: A dual-descriptor predictive approach that incorporates measures of nano-scale chemical short-range order (SRO) and vibrational disorder will enable the identification of HEAs with inherently low phonon thermal conductivity, by leveraging the additional phonon scattering induced by sub-micron chemical clustering.
fields.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys produced as single-phase solid solutions by arc melting, where traditional models primarily addressing average compositional metrics have been used.
fields.intervention: Enhance the predictive model by adding descriptors quantifying the extent of chemical short-range ordering (using, for example, indicators derived from pair correlation functions or scattering parameters) alongside vibrational disorder metrics (such as mass variance). These descriptors should be integrated into the GA’s fitness function to guide the optimization toward compositions that favor nano-scale clustering.
fields.conditions: Applicable to HEAs that are processed to ensure minimal macro segregation (e.g., through repeated remelting) so that any detected chemical ordering is at the nano-scale. Subsequent experimental characterization must include high-resolution microscopy (TEM/EDS) and phonon thermal conductivity measurements (laser flash or time-domain thermoreflectance) at room temperature.
fields.structural_mediator: Nano-scale chemical clusters act as additional scattering centers for phonons, thereby shortening the phonon mean free path without necessarily compromising overall phase stability and mechanical properties.
fields.mechanism: Even in an overall single-phase alloy, subtle short-range order can result in regions of slightly different bonding environments. This heterogeneous structure increases phonon scattering, and when combined with inherent vibrational disorder due to mass mismatch, leads to a lower lattice thermal conductivity.
fields.predicted_outcome: The predictive approach is expected to identify HEA compositions that, when synthesized, exhibit a reduction in phonon thermal conductivity of roughly 15% or more compared to alloys selected without consideration of SRO, while maintaining acceptable mechanical integrity.
fields.baseline: Standard predictive models that optimize alloy properties based solely on average metrics (mixing enthalpy, entropy, VEC) without explicit consideration of nano-scale chemical ordering.
fields.boundary: This hypothesis applies mainly to single-phase HEAs where nano-scale chemical ordering can occur without triggering macroscopic phase separation. In alloys that form distinct secondary phases, the correlation between SRO descriptors and phonon scattering may not hold.
fields.uncertainty: The quantification of nano-scale SRO in disordered alloys is challenging, and the degree to which it affects phonon transport relative to other scattering mechanisms is not precisely known.

falsification_experiment.design: Implement the enhanced predictive model to screen for HEAs predicted to exhibit significant nano-scale SRO and high vibrational disorder. Synthesize a subset of these alloys and perform detailed microstructural analysis using TEM/EDS to quantify SRO, then measure their phonon thermal conductivity and compare with control alloys chosen using traditional models.
measurements: Phonon thermal conductivity
Nano-scale chemical ordering (TEM, atom probe tomography)
Overall phase purity (XRD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If alloys selected using the dual-descriptor approach do not show a statistically significant decrease (≥15% reduction) in phonon thermal conductivity compared to controls, or if TEM analyses fail to reveal enhanced nano-scale SRO, the hypothesis is falsified.
